findings.text: Anonymous folio handling requires agreement between swap backing and swap cache presence, treating disagreement as unexpected and aborting without changes. Folios without swap backing follow a lazy free path, while swap backed folios are handled one page at a time in the observed logic.

Unmapping distinguishes stable outcomes for a cleared entry: swap installation for anonymous content, accounting adjustment for file backed content, poison replacement when poison handling is requested, and silent discard when content is marked unneeded and fault tracking is absent. Coverage of a whole folio permits early end of the walk.

Locked areas normally prevent unmapping and force a failure indication. When all entries for the folio have been seen under protection without crossing a table boundary, the lock state is restored and the walk ends. Partial observation under a locked area continues scanning instead of aborting at once.

When no leaf entry is found during unmap, lazy free state triggers an attempt at huge removal with distinct success and abort results, while a split request causes temporary release of table protection followed by a split and a restart without that request. A persisting absence of a leaf beyond those cases is treated as an internal inconsistency.

Both unmap and migrate walks offer a synchronous mode that waits for concurrent table reclamation on another processor. Without it a concurrent clear and reverse mapping removal may let the operation return before mapped state becomes false. Selection is per operation through its option flags.

Migration installs a special entry that records the page location and preserves earlier attributes. Writability selects a writable form, exclusive anonymous state selects an exclusive readable form, otherwise a plain readable form is used. Youth, dirtiness, soft dirtiness and fault tracking markers are carried over through separate handling for previously present and previously non present entries.

Shared huge table handling during migration for file backed folios requires the area lock before the mapping lock, with only a try acquisition attempted in this path and failure aborting the operation. Gather and flush surround the unshare attempt, and a successful unshare ends the walk because the folio is already unmapped.

Unmap and migrate may record a pending invalidation instead of invalidating immediately when deferral is requested. Correctness then relies on architecture guarantees that a clean to dirty transition on a cached entry becomes visible and traps once unmapped, since a remote processor might otherwise keep writing after the clear.
Temporary stack areas count as invalid for migration purposes. Separately a folio counts as not mapped exactly when its mapped indication is false.

Device exclusive conversion takes an address space, an address, an owner token for notification filtering, and a folio output location. It faults the page writable with huge split handling, rejects non anonymous or huge folios with an unsupported error, and on success returns the page while reporting the locked folio through the output.

Device exclusive conversion requires the address space lock to be held on entry and acquires the folio lock interruptibly, reporting interruption as failure. Cache maintenance, table clearing and marker installation occur while the folio stays locked and secondary notifications are active.

Device exclusive conversion notifies secondary users of exclusive intent and then revalidates that the same folio and page remain mapped writable at leaf level. Any mismatch in identity, depth or writability causes notification closure, unlock and release followed by a fresh retry from faulting. Callers must filter their own owner token to avoid self induced livelock.

Read only data validation confirms that a known sample still holds its expected value, that a faulting write attempt is rejected, that the sample is unchanged afterwards, and that both ends of the read only section are page aligned. Any failure is logged and stops further checks, while complete success is logged once.
TEST_VALUE denotes the integer 195 used to initialize and validate the read only sample.
SECRETMEM_MODE_MASK denotes zero, and SECRETMEM_FLAGS_MASK denotes the same value as the mode mask, indicating no mode bits are currently defined.
Secret memory defaults to enabled with a true initial state that is protected from modification after initialization completes.

Discard of unneeded content is suppressed when fault handling is armed on the area, avoiding unexpected faults during copy style use. Write protection tracking from fault handling is preserved across unmap and migrate through marker installation or flag carry.
Successful removals reduce reverse mapping counts, drain per processor lock state for locked areas, and release references. High water accounting is updated before resident counts are lowered.
Logging in the read only test and in secret memory uses per file prefixes that identify the subsystem emitting each message.
